# HM-IBF-ROBO

> A hyper-heuristic that **designs** island-model metaheuristics, and a 6-DOF robot trajectory benchmark to design them for. The Cargo workspace holds `grahf`, a framework whose search space is a *graph of islands* — node weights pick each island's metaheuristic, edge weights pick the migration policy, IRACE tunes every candidate — and `grahf-robo`, the robotics benchmark built on it, plus the `hm-ibf` pipeline binary and a Python instance generator. Written in Rust (2021 edition) and Python, licensed `GPL-3.0-or-later`.

What separates it from a homogeneous island model: islands run at **different dimensions** (`dimensions_allowed = [6, 12, 18, 24, 30]`, i.e. `1, 2, 3, 4, 5` joint waypoints of a 6-DOF arm). A solution is a flattened vector of joint angles, six per waypoint, with linear motion in joint space between waypoints; a migrant crossing to an island of another dimension is *resampled* after projecting its waypoints onto the shortest Cartesian route through the instance's targets, never padded or truncated.

Execution is Docker-only. `./run.sh` (macOS/Linux/Git Bash) or `.\run.bat` (PowerShell/cmd) builds the image, starts the container and forwards commands; `./run.sh verify` is the definition of done. The pipeline is **preprocess → train → evaluate** with no manual steps: `python3 -m preprocessing.prepare_instances` (from `hm-ibf-robo/`), then `hm-ibf train`, `hm-ibf evaluate` (or `hm-ibf pipeline`). Training shells out to R/IRACE and needs the Nix-enabled image (`HM_IBF_NIX=1`).

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/README.md): project overview, requirements, the three pipeline stages, end-to-end smoke test, repository layout, retargeting to another problem (~2k tokens)
- [Benchmark design](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/hm-ibf-robo/README.md): the trajectory problem and objective function, island node-weight encoding, the heterogeneous migration transform, the verbatim best-individual export (~1k tokens)
- [Runbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/hm-ibf-robo/runbook.md): operational detail per stage, the CLI flags with their defaults, tuning parameters, stage outputs, the transform catalog (~2k tokens)
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/AGENTS.md): the contributor and coding-agent contract — Docker-only execution, Google-style doc comments, test layout, 500-line file limit, verification gate, plus a full project guide for agents (~6k tokens)

## Configuration

- [params_training.conf](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/params_training.conf): TOML tuning parameters of the `train`/`pipeline` stage, including `dimensions_allowed` and the shared `max_evaluations` budget
- [params_evaluation.conf](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/params_evaluation.conf): TOML tuning parameters of the `evaluate`/`pipeline` stage
- [Dockerfile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/Dockerfile): the single sanctioned execution environment; multi-stage, non-root, `dev` and `dev-nix` targets
- [flake.nix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/flake.nix): Nix devshell providing R/IRACE for the training stage
- [Cargo.toml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/Cargo.toml): workspace manifest and Rust dependencies
- [pyproject.toml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/pyproject.toml): `ruff` and `pytest` configuration for the Python side

## Source

- [src/](https://github.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/tree/main/src): the `grahf` framework — graph operators, island executor, migration transform trait, the algorithm-design problem and its IRACE tuning
- [hm-ibf-robo/src/](https://github.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/tree/main/hm-ibf-robo/src): the `grahf-robo` library and `hm-ibf-robo` binary — CLI, config loading, training, evaluation, the trajectory problem and its evaluator, island and migration builders, the dimension transforms
- [hm-ibf-robo/preprocessing/](https://github.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/tree/main/hm-ibf-robo/preprocessing): the Python instance generator — deterministic point selection from the upstream `Pos_pnts.mat` point cloud, mirroring `EvoApps2023/main.m`, plus the on-demand shallow clone that fetches it
- [hm-ibf-robo/instances/](https://github.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/tree/main/hm-ibf-robo/instances): the 40 checked-in benchmark instances — `nr_points in {3, 4, 5, 6}` times ten instance seeds — plus their `summary.json`
- [scripts/](https://github.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/tree/main/scripts): the in-container `hm-ibf` shim and the verification gate

## Agent skills

- [hm-ibf-audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/.claude/skills/hm-ibf-audit/SKILL.md): classifies any source tree against the HM-IBF definition and reports where it deviates (~2k tokens)
- [hm-ibf-retarget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/.claude/skills/hm-ibf-retarget/SKILL.md): the ordered edit surface for swapping in another optimization problem, with a domain fit test and a `--check` pass for leftover robotics assumptions (~3k tokens)

## Optional

- [LICENSE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/main/LICENSE): GNU General Public License v3.0 or later, full text
- [Tests](https://github.com/anonymous.4open.science/HM-IBF-ROBO/tree/main/hm-ibf-robo/tests): the Rust pipeline integration tests and the pytest suite for the preprocessing package
- [Robotics-Benchmarking](https://github.com/JakubKudela89/Robotics-Benchmarking): upstream repository supplying `Pos_pnts.mat` and the MATLAB point-selection reference
- [MAHF](https://github.com/mahf-opt/mahf): the metaheuristics framework `grahf` builds on
- [irace-rs](https://github.com/Saethox/irace-rs): the Rust bindings to IRACE used for parameter tuning
